Indian Standard
SPECIFICATION FOR METAL LASTS FOR KNEE BOOTS
0. FOREWORD 0.1This Indian Standard was adopted by the Indian Standards Institution
on 5 October 1981, after the draft finalized by the Footwear Sectional Committee, had been approved by the Chemical Division Council. 0.2 A Series of Indian Standards on lasts is being compiled for grinding manufactures of lasts and footwear. The principles on which this standard, the fourth in the series, is based are given below. 0.3 Two-third from the rear, including the leg height portion, is concerned with the least mobile part of the feet; as such this portion need not change with fashion or for a specific requirement. It is mainly the fore-part, its shape and the length of the insole from ball to toe to the last that alter with fashion. The modern factory practice is to standardize the back portion (approximately 2/3 between heel and ball) for a particular heel height. 0.4 From the designing point of view it is not desirable to lay down any rigorous specification either for the shape or distribution of material on last; only the dimensional aspect is followed, with guidance on material, mechanical requirements, sampling and test methods as well as various constructions1 requirements of the metal lasts for knee boots. 0.5 In this standard, as far as feasible, rationalized vaIues of English sizes, which are in vouge in India have been prescribed. Equivalent Paris points shall be in accordance with IS : 1638-1969". It is hoped that the footwear industry which is presently following English sizes or Paris points or both will progressively switch over to an internationally acknowledged rational metric size system. The Sectional Committee further took note of the `Mondopoint' as a possible solution in the future for size and fitting standardization in the metric system, but decided not to prescribe this system in this specification in view of its being still in the developmental stage. 0.6 For the purpose of deciding whether a particular requirement of this standard is complied with, the final value, observed or calculated, expressing the result of a test or analysis, shall be rounded off in accordance with IS : 2-1960t. The number of significant places retained in the rounded off value should be the same as that of the specified value in this standard.

1. SCOPE 1.1 This standard specifies the requirements and methods of sampling and test for metallic last used for the manufacture of knee boots. 2. TERMINOLOGY 2.1 For the purpose of this standard, the definitions given in 1967* shall apply.

3. REQUIREMENTS 3. I Materials - A suitable aluminium alloy (see Note) shall be used for the manufacture of the lasts.
alloy NOTE- Aluminium may be used for the purpose. ingots conforming to Designation A-4 of IS

: 617-1975t

3.1.1 Last Pins - shall be one-piece made from mild steel of basic size and dimensions as shown in Fig. 1.

IS : 10089 - 1981 3.1.2 M S Wire - shall be of 3 mm diameter made from MS and its length shall be 2 mm more than the top thickness of the last.

3.1.3 Pointed Pins (Striper ) -- shall be of 3 mm diameter made from mild steel with a pointed edge on one side and length of 10 to 12 mm.
NOTE- This pin on the top of aluminium last is used only in big organized industry where vulcanising racks, trolley, semi or fully automatic conveyor fitted with holder which correspondingly hold the aluminium lasts with the help of pins, during various mechanised manufacturing process, are used.

3.1.4 MS Rod .- for holding the fore-part of the last in dove-tail articulation ( locking) system shall be 3 mm in diameter and made from mild steel. 3.2 Construction and Finish 3.2.1 The last shall be hollow cast by sand casting, diecasting or centrifugal casting. 3.2.2 The lasts shall be free from blowholes, depressions, casting marks and other surface defects. Tiny blowholes may, however, be permissible. 3.2.3 The pattern of knee boots shall be made in two pieces so that the last can be cast from aluminium in two parts-front and the back-including the leg part. Both these sections after casting shall be joined together with any type of suitable locking, namely: a) Dovetail method, b) Spring lock system, and c) Cone locking system. 3.2.4 To enable easy unlasting of the knee boot after vulcanisation, the locking system shall be such that the leg part can be lifted upward and bent in order to have the operation of lasts slipping easy. A general guidance is given in Fig. 2.
NOTE - As knee boot is a high legged one piece footwear (made of rubber upper and fabric lining), detachable or articulated lasts are preferable both in organized and small scale industries in order to achieve quality finish of the footwear and also the chance of tear white unlasting.

3.2.5 Fixing of Pins - The pins shall be inserted either while casting or after casting by drilling a corresponding hole at the surface of the last, then pushing the pin through the hole with the help of oil. The pins shall then be rivetted through and through with last comb surface with a 3-mm thick MS wire. The position of the pins shall be such that the clip slot should face the rear of the last and along the middle longitudinal line of the top at equal distance from the outer side edges of the top as shown in Fig. 3.

3.2.6 The longitudinal axis of the pin shall be perpendicular to the plane of the top. 5

3.2.7 The distance from the centre of the pin up to the rear edge of the comb top shall be 4 mm for all : adults and adolescent ( size 2 to 12 ) and 30 mm for children's sizes. The tolerance shall be f 2 mm. 3.2.8 The striper ( pointed needle shall be fixed about 5 mm deep inside the last wall along the wedge shaped cut-out which needs to be grooved along the last leg .surface as per the demand of the height of the boot. The strap edge shall not be exposed 5 mm more than the surface in order to reduce handling hazard. The width and the shape of the groove are given in Fig. 3 and 4. The height on the leg of the last for engraving the groove shall be generally 25 to 33 mm above the top line of the rubber upper.
NOTEThese edge pins are required to hold the fabric lining of the boot in Then rubber uppers are put over this stretching condition during the lasting process. fabric lining. After completion of the boot ( lasting, putting foxing, sole heel, etc ) and just before sending them to vulcanizing boiler, tlus extra fabric lining is cut-off along the top line. This method of stretching the lining along with the upper gives a faultless finish of the boot.

3.2.9 The articulated parts either by way of dove-tail or any other system shall be firmly fixed and shall be of sufficient resistance, strength and efficient mechanism so that by stretching, lifting on in normal position the last shall not wobble. The MS wire ( pin) holding the fore-part while lifting ( stretching ) shall be of adequate strength and shall be rivetted flush to the body of the last and not project outside, which may cause damage to the boot.

IS : 10089 - 1981 3.2.10 The pins shall be inserted tightly flush with the top vertically at 90" directing the clip slots always towards the back of the last and the diameter and depth of the hole `B' shall correspond to the outside diameter and height of the pin. The diameter and depth of the hole `A' shall precisely correspond to the diameter and length of the pin (Fig. 2).

3.2.11 The MS wire by which the pin is tivetted to the body of last through hole `B' shall be fIushed and not project outside. 3.2.12 On all lasts, pin-points shall be punched for check up of their dimensions. These measuring points are put accurately in locations as follows: a) In the fore-part of the last, 3 pin-points shall be put, the first at the inside joint, the second at the outside joint and the third at the base of the instep (along the centre line of the comb or last). The measurement of the joint girths of the last shall be carried out through these 3 points. b) The number of pin-points on the instep of the last for measuring the instep girth shall be one only. c) The number of pin-points to be punched along the middle line of the last and leg back curve shall be at intervals as shown in Fig. 5. These various heights shall be measured vertically from the back height by putting the last on a flat-plain surface (without any heels, see Fig. 5). Now with the help of these point-marks measuring tape shall be placed flat on the surface of the last leg body, parallel to the top line. For easy placing of the tape, a few more point marks may be punched along these lines. 3.2.13 Lasts shall be evenly, accurately and correctly scoured (ground} as per templates and measurements, first by 60 grit and then finally by 100 grit abrasive. The surface of the last shall be absolutely smooth and glazed (polished) for easy unlasting of boots after vulcanisation. No casting defects or marks shall be visible. Lasts of identical sizes and fittings shall conjugate, that is, the right band last shall, in respect of form, serve as mirror image of the left hand one.
NOTE - Before starting finishing jobs, lasts should be received from casting in such a condition that there shall be no casting defects, namely, shrinkage, contraction, depression or blowholes.

3.2.14 The pin and the top of the last shall be coloured with quick drying aluminium paint ( see IS : 2339-1963* ) which shall withstand vulcanising temperature up to 150�C for 1 h.

3.3 Design 3.3.1 The constructidn or modelling ( designing) of knee boot last shall be subject to agreement between the purchaser and tbe supplier on specific

Is:10089-1981 requirement with the help of dimensions given in Fig. 4. Even the length of the insole may vary on the basis of toe shape. A guideline is being provided (see Appendix A ) for insole construction. For a very wide toe it may be one half size less than the standard insole length and for a pointed toe it may be again one half size longer than the standard insole length. 3.3.2 Although minimum requirements are being provided in the Table of Fig. 5 and the maximum limit subject to agreement between the purchaser and the supplier, for economy reasons one common insole pattern can be used for two fittings. In this case insole pattern shall be designed on the basis of bigger fittings. NOTE-The initial model last itself, when designed, should have an adequate
amount of `overhang' around the sides. This feature facilitates the subsequent modelling of the other fittings by adjustment of the wood above the insole feather edge.

3.4 Dimensions of Last 3.4.1 The length, size, width, fittings and other measurements shall conform to the minimum specifications given in Table 1, Fig. 4. and Fig. 6.
NOTE - The percentage of any individual fitting of the lasts, with maximum specification, that is. more than that of minimum specification of Table 1 and Fig. 5 according to sizea, shall be subject to agreement between the supplier and the purchaser.

3.5 Wall Thickness 3.5.1 The wall thickness in different portions ( sections) of the aluminium last shall be as follows ( see Fig. 4) a) Planter ( bottom or sole ) = 5 mm ( -fr O-5 mm ) b) Dorsal ( front or top or upper ) = 4 mm ( f 05 mm) c) Comb top = 32 mm (-& 0.1 mm ) 3.6 Permissible Deviations in Dimensions 3.6.1 In the production of knee boot aluminium lasts, the dimensions of the fore-part may have tolerance f 0.5 mm. 3.6.2 The dimensions of the other surface ( namely, heal to ankle, different leg heights, girths) may have tolerance f 1 mm. 3.6.3 In the case of insole feather edge or sole shape maximum f 0.3 mm tolerance all round shall be permissible. 4. 13

IS : 10089 - 1981 5. PACKING 5.1 Lasts shall be properly packed in boxes made of wooden planks ( see IS : 1503-1967"). 5.1.1 The case shall be lined with ,waterproof packing paper ( see IS : 1398-19687 ) along bottom and sides. A layer of shavings or straw shall then be spread on the paper at the bottom of the case and a suitable number of lasts placed in rows. The space between individual lasts and between the lasts and the sides of the case shall be filled closely with paper cuttings, wood shavings or straw. On the lasts so arranged, a layer of wood shavings, straw or paper cuttings shall be spread. In this way layers of last shall be packed till the box is filled. The top layer shall also be covered with straw, wood shavings or paper cutting and the packing paper. 5.1.2 Nails fixing the cover lid, shall be correctly driven in and shall not come out from the boards on the inner or outer surface of the box. 5.1.3 The cases shall be secured against breakage in transit by binding with hoop iron or similar devices. 5.1.4 In the case of card board boxes, they shall be secured by nylon strapping and corresponding metal seal and finally covered with gunny bags. 6. SAMPLING AND CRITERIA FOR CONFORMITY

6.1 For the purpose of ascertaining the conformity of the lasts for safety rubber knee boots to this specification, the scale of sampling and criteria for conformity shall be as given in Appendix B. 7. TEST METHODS 7.1 Visual Characteristicr - Examine the last visually for conformity to the approved specimen in respect of finish, appearance, surface defects, etc. 7.2 Dimensional Characteristics 7.2.1 Determine the length of the lasts by size-stick, based on the standard length as given in Table 1. 7.2.2 To ensure that the longitudinal and transverse sections as well as ball and heel parts and bottom shape of any size in a set of lasts agree with the specifications for shape and measurements, use graded insole patterns and various graded control profiles, including back curve of the heel leg, toe and bottom profile for the entire size range.
NOTE-The patterns for insole and profiles shall be cut to the master or model size, It gives length, shape, width of the from which the remaining sizes shall be graded. fore-part seat and leg and to this extent it is suitable for testing the lasts. Grades are fixed arbitrarily and adopted by custom in the last industry. *Specification iSpecification for wooden for packing packing cases ( sceondrcvision ). paper, waterproof, bituman-laminated

(first rcui~ion ).

14

IS :10089-1981 7.2.2.1 On superimposition, the profile pattern of the longitudinal bottom section ( generally called `bottom profile' ) shall coincide with the axis of the last along with the contour of the heel back curve.
7.2.2.2 On superimposition, the profile pattern of the longitudinal leg section ( generally called `back profile' ) shall coincide with the axis of the last along with the contour of the back heel up to the top of the leg. 7.2.2.3 On superimposition, the profile section of the longitudinal toe section ( generally called `toe profile') shall coincide with the longitudinal axis of the body of the last in its upper fore-part. 7.2.3 Carry out measurement of the last with standard last measuring tape ( a tape of non-variable dimensions with fine metallic wire inside) the width of the tape shall not be more than 10 mm.

7.2.4 During measurement of joint, instep, ankle and different leg height lay the measuring tape on the last in such a way that the measuring edge of the tape fits closely and lies fiat on the last along the line of measurement.
7.2.4.1 During measurement of instep girth of the lasts, the measuring edge of the tape of the comb shall come in contact with the marked point. Near the bottom, the tape shall settle in the most concave part of the last in such a manner as to give (during this measurement of the last ) the smaIIest size. 7.2.5 Determine Fis. 6 "standard Appendix A. the location of the joint for insole construction" /++-2Omm measurements as shown in and description given in

INSOLE CONSTRUCTION

IS : 10089- 1981 7.2.5.1 Approximate position for location of the ball and instep girth measurement in insole pattern is shown in Fig. 4. This system requires little skill and may be performed very easily without the help of any apparatus and as such may be considered as standard practice under the existing conditions.
NOTE- Although the joint girth measurement is taken diagonally in a transverse direction, but makers of lasts take thii measurement at arbitrary points; this enables them to place the measuring tape Rat to the wood of the last. Generally this takes in either the inside or outside joint, but never both.

7.2.6 Following the system described above, check the correctness of position of pin-points in this manner; the bottom of the last, the insole, checked by marked lines is superimposed, so that starting from the toe part, it coincides all over with the bottom of the last. 7.2.6.1 Pin-points at the joints ( inside and outside) shall be exactly located on the last at the ends of lines above the counter ( feather edge ) of the lasts at a distance of 10 mm. 7.2.6.2 Correctness of the position of the pin-points located on the body of the last at the base of the instep ( along with centre line of the last ) is checked either with the measuring tape with the help of two pin-points of the joints for measurement of the ball girth; or by the longitudinal front profile which with the mark point is put on the last and the coincidence of the pin-point on the last with the point of the profile is observed. 7.2.7 For the determination of the correctness of the position of the pin-point for measurement of instep girth on the cone of the last, the following method is recommended. 7.2.7.1 This position is represented on the last, along with the middle of the cone, at a distance of 60 mm above the ball joint pin-point which is located at the base of the instep ( cone ) ( see Fig. 5 ). 7.2.7.2 To ascertain the girth of the instep, the tape shall lie flat and close to the last on the selected points.
NOTE - Like the joint measurement the instep measurement may not also be located exactly by rule. Half standard length of the last (excluding the difference between the length of the insole and the foot), on an imaginary line through the length may be The largest girth at that point probably answer given as the approximate position. the purpose best.

7.2.8 To ascertain the girth of the ankle, the tape shall lie flat around the heel seat and ankle, as shown in Fig. 4 and 5. 7.2.9 To ascertain the girth of the leg at 10, 20, 30 and 40 cm, the tape shall lie flat as shown in Fig. 5 and parallel to the top line.
NOTE-Leg height shall be determined by placing the last on a flat surface (without putting cny heel ) and measuring vertically from the heel seat point at the required height.

16

fS : 10089 - 1981 7.2.10 Check-up of the Insole Pattern of Medium Size - In order to check the basic dimensions of the insole, it is necessary to determine the position of points of measurement.

7.2.10.1 Determine the position of measurement by a special pattern or template, the construction of which is given in Fig. 6 and Appendix A. 7.2.10.2 Test beforehand carefully graded patterns of insole, proiile templates of longitudinal and transverse sections, used for check up for the lasts.
NOTE - The actual or stick-length of last may vary from the standard length of the insole pattern. The insole length shall be always 2 and 3 mm shorter than the sticklength by virtue of the back curve protruding behind it and the accepted sticklength of a last is the distance from the centre of the curve at the back to the extreme tip of the toe. The actual size-stick length is not to be used to denote the foot fitting length of a last. For any given shoe or last size, the foot shall be shorter than the insole by at least 10 mm when measurement is taken in a sitting position.

7.2.11 Check the dimensions of the pin by caliper as well as by opposite holder. 7.2.12 Measurement of Heel Height - Place the last on a level surface. Raise the seat of the last until the tread line touches the level surface. Then measure the heel height from the seat position to the level surface. Take care that the seat of the last rests almost parallel to the ground. 7.2.13 Measurement of Toe Spring - The distance between the tip of toe and the level surface where the last is placed on the required heel and parallel to the ground is the required toe spring. 7.2.14 For all sizes, the height of heel and toe spring shall be 25 mm and 2.5 mm respectively or as per agreement between the purchaser and the supplier. 7.215 For all sizes, the height of the last shall be same and as per table given in Fig. 5 or as per agreement between the purchaser and the supplier. 7.3 Mechanical and Other Requirements The following items shall be tested for mechanical and other requirements by cutting or opening up the lasts drawn at random from those already tested ( see B-2.1.3.1 ) in accordance with co1 4 and 6 of Table 2. a) Wall thickness of the last and physical properties of the material used. Dimension of the pin. b) c) Proper fitting of the pin. proper fitting, quality and shape ( needed for locking d) Spring-Its arrangement ). 17

IS : 10089 - 1981 7.3.1 Examine the position of the pin as well as the hole for the holder vertical to the surface of the heel and the distance for the centre of pin hole as per sketch.

DESIGNING OF INSOLE DRAFT A-l. DIRECTIONS FOR THE DESIGN A-l.1 The design of insole of the last and its shape shall be as given in Fig. 7 with the constructional details given below : AB = Absolute insole length AD = Foot sole length BD = Absolute addition C = Intersection of the joint measuring line with the middle line. AC = 213 AB. Draw transverse line EF through C making an angle of 90" with AB (EF = width of ball or tread width ) FF1 = 2 cm. and EFF 1 = 90" Take the ball measurement by tape along line EF,. J = Point for the heel measuring line AJ ~1 l/6 AD (JK = width of heel) and depends on fitting. M =-Draw a straight line through J from A at a distance of 15 mm from C on the ball line EF. This is the axis of symmetry for heel end. CEG .= Big toe angle. Draw a line from E in the toe direction making an angle of 80" with EF. This line intersects the transverse line through D at G. CFH E: Small toe angle. Draw a line from F in the toe direction making an angle of 80" with EF. This line intersects the transverse line through D at IT. 2 = Small toe point. This point is marked on FH such that FZ = 10 percent of AD. D = Toe height ( with bottom iron plated last ). The height of toe is the same for all widths. S - Height of the heel = 16 mm. T = Toe spring = 16 mm. 18

APPENDIX ( Clause 6.1)

B

SCALE OFSAMPLINGANDCRITERIAF~RC~NF~RMITY B-l, SAMPLINGOFFOOTWEARLASTS B-l.1 Lot-All last pairs in a consignment
of the same style, type, size and fitting and belonging to the same batch of manufacture shall be grouped together to constitute a lot.

B-l.2 For ascertaining the conformity of the lot to the requirements of this specification, tests shall be carried out for each lot separately. The number of last pairs, to be drawn from any lot shall depend on the size of the lot and shall be in accordance with co1 1 and 2 of Table 2. B-l.3 Such pairs shall be selected at randon from the lot and in order to ensure the randomness of selection, a random number table (see IS: 4905 - 1968" ) shall be used. In case such a table is not available, the following procedure shall be used:

IS : 10089 - 1981

Arrange all the pairs in the lot in a systematic manner and starting from any pair, count them as 1, 2, 3,. . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . up to r and so on in one order, where r is the integral part of N/n ( N being the total number of pairs in the lot and n being, the number of pairs to be selected in the sample). Every rth pair thus counted shall be withdrawn to give the sample for test. B-2. NUMBER OF TESTS AND CRITERIA FQR CONFORMITY

B-2.1 Number of Tests B-2.1.1 Defective Last - A last which, has one or more defects with respect to a quality characteristic under consideration shall be considered a defective last. B-2.1.2 All the pairs selected under B-l.3 shall be first examined for visual characteristics. If the number of pairs failing to satisfy these requirements for each characteristic is less than or equal to the corresponding permissible number of defectives given in co1 3 of Table 2, the lot shall be declared to have satisfied the requirements for these characteristics. If, however, the number of defective pairs exceeds the permissible number, the lot shall be considered as not conforming to the requirements for these characteristics. B-2.1.3 Dimensional Characteristics - The lot which has been found satisfactory as in B-2.1.2 shall next be tested for dimensional characteristics. B-2.1.3.1 The pairs for this purpose shall be taken from those already drawn ( see B-1.3 ) in accordance with co1 2 and 4 of Table 2. These pairs shall be taken at random and tested for the dimensional characteristics as specified in the relevant clauses. If the number of pairs failing to satisfy the requirements for these characteristics is less than or equal to the corresponding numbergiven in co1 5 of Table 2, the lot shall be declared to have satisfied the requirements for these characteristics, otherwise not. B-2.1.4 ikfechanical Characteristics - The lot which has been found satisfactory for visual and dimensional characteristics shall then be tested for mechanical characteristics ( see 7.3 to 7.3.1). For this purpose, the pairs shall be drawn at random in accordance with co1 6 of Table 2 from those selected for the purpose of B-2.2.2. The lot shall be considered to be satisfactory in respect of these characteristics, if all the selected pairs satisfy the requirements for these characteristics. B-2.1.4.1 The lot shall be considered to have satisfied the requirements of dimensional and mechanical characteristics of the component parts if the selected pairs pass all the tests prescribed for these properties. B-2.2 Criteria for Conformity B-2.2.1 The lot shall be declared as conforming to all the requirements of this specification if it passes in B-2.1.1, B-2.1.2, B-2.1.3 and B-2.1.4. 21
